01 / A LITTLE CONTEXT

Learning the craft.
Keeping people in mind.

I’m pursuing software engineering because I want to turn ideas into things people can use. Right now, that means learning the foundations, asking questions, and connecting the small steps to a bigger goal.

One idea keeps me curious: an AI people can talk to in Rohingya. It brings together my interest in technology and a language that matters to me. This is where I’m beginning.

PROJECT BRIEF / 001

CONCEPT STAGE

Rohingya Voice.

A personal project idea by Serazul Hoque: let people talk to AI in Rohingya.

The ambition

Create a simple voice-first conversation experience that puts a familiar language at the center. The first version should be narrow enough to evaluate with real speakers.

A proposed approach

Explore speech input, an existing AI model, and spoken output. First assess Rohingya support, accuracy, data needs, and whether the available tools can support a useful prototype.

What success could look like

A speaker can ask one everyday question and understand the response. Review with Rohingya speakers should guide the next step.

This brief describes a proposed direction and an initial prototype goal.
